questions.question: In which part of the excretory system of the human body urine is it stored before passing urine?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The urine is stored in the **urinary bladder**__ before passing out.
 
• The **urethra **is a tube that connects the urinary bladder to the urethral meatus.
 
• **91-96% of urine consists of water** it also includes proteins, hormones and salts
 
• Urine is pale yellow due to the result of a pigment called __**urochrome.**__
 
• The ureter carries urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.
 
• Bowman's Capsule helps in the** filtration of blood to form urine.**

questions.question: Which side of the human heart receives abundant oxygen-rich blood from the lungs?
questions.solution:
__

• The **pulmonary veins** channels oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium.
 
• The **inferior and superior vena cava** brings the **oxygen-poor blood** from the body into the **right atrium.**
 
• The **pulmonary artery** brings oxygen-poor blood from the **right ventricle **into the lungs.

questions.question: Which international organisation governs basketball in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**FIBA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **FIBA **governs the game of basketball in the world.
 
• Its Full form is **Federation Internationale de Basketball.**
 
• **FIBA **is Headquartered in **Mies, Switzerland.**
 
• Founded in **1932**, it brings together **213 National Basketball Federations from all over the world.**
 
• There are **5 players**__ in a **basketball **team.
 
• It is played between two teams of five players each on a **rectangular court, usually indoors. **
 
• Each team tries to score by tossing the ball through the opponent’s goal, an elevated horizontal hoop and net called a** basket.**
 
• The court is divided into two main sections by the **mid-court line.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__** 

**IBA (International Boxing Association)**

 
• Worldwide governing body for amateur boxing.
 
• Oversees international competitions and sets rules for amateur boxing.
 
• Ensures safety and fairness in the sport globally.
 
• Known earlier as AIBA (Association Internationale de Boxe Amateur).
 
• Involves in the promotion and development of boxing worldwide.

**RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia)**

 
• Australia's central bank.
 
• Manages the country's monetary policy.
 
• Responsible for the issuance of currency.
 
• Aims to maintain the financial system's stability.
 
• Not directly related to sports but mentioned for clarity due to its popular acronym.

**NBA (National Basketball Association)**

 
• Premier professional basketball league in North America, highly recognized globally.
 
• Consists of 30 teams (29 in the US and 1 in Canada).
 
• Known for having some of the world's best-paid athletes.
 
• Established in 1946 as the Basketball Association of America (BAA); became NBA in 1949 after merging with the National Basketball League (NBL).
 
• Renowned for high competition levels, global popularity, and significant influence in professional sports.

questions.question: Image formed by Plane Mirror is always ________.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Plane Mirror: A plane mirror is a mirror with a flat (planar) reflective surface.

The characteristics of an image formed in a plane mirror:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13ff2a7e1be1cb854b8dd08c9c6ab537716e1426fe3d497995587e5c7304852.png] 

 
• The image formed by the plane mirror is virtual and erect i.e. image cannot be projected or focused on a screen.
 
• The distance of the image ‘behind’ the mirror is the same as the distance of the object in front of the mirror.
 
• The size of the image formed is the same as the size of the object.
 
• The image is laterally inverted, i.e. left hand appears to be right hand when seen from the plane mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d092687faf74746b566b59e1e432f1ba5504516fa974143e619ab92dbc19c55.png] 

 
• If the object moves towards (or away from) the mirror at a certain rate, the image also moves towards (or away from) the mirror at the same rate.

EXPLANATION__:

From the above discussion, we can say that,

 
• The **image formed by Plane Mirror is always** **Virtual and Erect. **So option 1 is correct.
 
• A **convex lens and a concave mirror** forms both real and virtual images.
 
• A **concave lens and a convex mirror** can form only virtual images.

questions.question: "Any body that is completely or partially submerged in a ﬂuid (gas or liquid) at rest is acted upon by an upward or buoyant force, the magnitude of which is equal to the weight of the ﬂuid displaced by the body." Which is this law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Archimedes' Principle**__

__Concept:__

Archimedes principle:

__
 
• The principle of Archimedes states “When a body is immersed in a liquid, an upward thrust, equal to the weight of the liquid displaced, acts on it.”

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/965af0fe078d8cd5de7d0224fb4dbf687b4efa01717a8d927db4a1b4462666bc.png] 

 
• Thus, when a solid is fully immersed in a liquid, it loses weight which is equal to the weight of the liquid it displaces.

Apparent weight = Actual weight - boyant force = mg - ρgV

Where m is mass of the object, ρ is the density of the fluid 

Hence if there is no gravity, there is no Upward Thrust.

The upward force applied to the object is called the buoyant force.

Here,

ρ = density of liquid

g = acceleration due to gravity

V = volume of liquid displaced by the object

 
• Archimedes Principle is also known as the physical law of buoyancy.
 
• The purity of gold in the king's crown, Archimedes determine after discovering the Archimedes principle.
 
• Hydrometers, Ships and Submarines work on the Archimedes Principle.
 
• A Ship/boat floats on the basis of the Archimedes Principle.

Explanation:__

__
 
• The **Archimedes' Principle__** states that "A body, that is completely or partially submerged in a ﬂuid (gas or liquid) at rest is acted upon by an upward or buoyant force, the magnitude of which is equal to the weight of the ﬂuid displaced by the body."
 
• The principle is used in Submarine, Hot-air balloons, Hydrometer.
 
• Charle's law states that at constant pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature.
 
• Boyle’s law states that the pressure exerted by a gas is inversely proportional to the volume occupied by the gas.

questions.question: The Narrow Zone of contact between land, air and water is called ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Narrow Zone of contact between land, air and water is called **Biosphere**__.
 
• There are three types of biospheres, as the lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere.
 
• The lithosphere is the rocky outer part of the Earth.
 
• The hydrosphere is the total amount of water present on a planet.
 
• The layers of gases around the earth completely form the atmosphere.
